About Figure

We’re Figure (Nasdaq: FIGR), and we’re building the future of capital markets with blockchain and AI. We make lending faster and cheaper for everyone by automating the origination process and using blockchain as the source of truth for loan ownership and connection to our capital marketplace.

It’s all one ecosystem that spans three lines of business:

  • Lending: HELOCs, cash-out refinance, DSCR loans, and crypto-backed loans for homeowners, investors, and small businesses. Through Kiavi, a Figure company, we also finance real estate investors with bridge, fix-and-flip, rental, and new construction loans.
  • Markets: On Figure Markets, people can lend and earn with Prime and $YLDS, an SEC-registered, interest-bearing security that settles like cash. OPEN is our blockchain infrastructure for issuing, distributing, and trading equities.
  • Partnerships: Banks, credit unions, fintechs, home improvement companies, and other lenders and brokers originate loans on our platform. DART records loan ownership on blockchain, and Figure Connect connects originators with institutional loan buyers.

See all of our products on figure.com.

Here’s where we are today:

  • $35B+ in equity unlocked for homeowners on Figure’s platform
  • 382K+ households served
  • 800+ B2B partners, including banks, credit unions, and fintechs
  • AAA-rated HELOC securitizations from S&P, KBRA, and Moody’s
  • $23B+ funded for real estate investors through Kiavi since 2013
  • Recognized by CNBC (World’s Top Fintech Companies 2026), Fortune (Crypto 100, 2026), and Inc. (2026 Inc. 5000)

If you want to help build the next era of lending, we’d love to meet you.

  • Governance and Board Reporting: Producing governance packs, MI, and reporting to a high standard for Committees, Risk Forums and other critical meetings, ensuring that stakeholder and regulatory needs are met, and distinguishing matters for information, discussion, decision and escalation.

Acting as Administrator of the system, overseeing access management and monitoring the quality of data.

What we need from you:

  • A solid background in enterprise risk, operational risk, or compliance within a fast-paced fintech, payments, or regulated financial services environment.
  • Proven experience in developing and embedding governance and policy frameworks, with the ability to identify and drive operational improvements.
  • Demonstrated tenacity and stakeholder management skills - we’re looking for someone who is comfortable holding senior leaders accountable to deadlines, quality, and action closure.
  • Experience producing executive, Board and committee reporting, translating complex technical information into clear business insights. 
  • Practical understanding of what ‘good’ looks like in policy architecture and internal control design (i.e. knowing how to translate high-level policy statements into verifiable, auditable controls).
  • Strong analytical capability, with experience interpreting data, identifying trends and recommending improvements that reduce risk and strengthen controls. 
  • Comfort working with data and reporting tools to build clean visual dashboards and extract trends and insights.
  • Experience using, implementing, or administering GRC platforms.
  • The ability to work independently and exercise your judgement to get stuff done. 
  • A keen attention to detail and an instinct of how to present information in a clear and digestible manner.

What you can expect from us:

  • Fair and competitive salary at every stage of your growth
  • Flexible working hours, with hybrid working at its heart
  • A culture built on passionate, growth-minded people
  • A flexible approach to holiday
  • Opportunities to travel to our offices around the world
  • An open and creative environment where you can help us define the future of BVNK, its culture, and its opportunity sets

At BVNK, we are focused on building a diverse and inclusive team. While you may not meet all of our requirements, we’d encourage you to apply if you meet the majority of our expectations. You may be a great fit for this role or another role in our team.

The Operations & Control Specialist supports the integrity, continuity and control of the Group's digital-asset platform workflows through operational verification, exception management, risk-sensitive case handling and cross-functional resolution.
 
The role requires practical knowledge of Digital Asset platform workflows and blockchain transactions. Substantial industry experience, particularly in understanding transaction workflows, investigating complex issues and coordinating cross-functional resolution, provides a strong foundation for this position. The Specialist applies this industry expertise to designated financial activities within The Group's established control framework.
 
Working across Finance, Asset, Operations and Technology functions, the position combines cryptocurrency business understanding with independent judgement, disciplined controls and accurate operational records.

Digital Asset Transaction Management

  • Execute designated digital asset activities with a focus on transaction integrity, accuracy and adherence to established financial controls.
  • Interpret blockchain transaction information and validate asset, network and transaction attributes against authorised business instructions and operational records.

  • Draw on knowledge of exchange transaction journeys to investigate discrepancies and distinguish processing or data issues from matters requiring technical investigation.
  • Coordinate with the relevant teams to resolve exceptions, documenting findings, actions taken and outstanding dependencies.
  • Communicate the financial and operational implications of unresolved issues clearly and follow up within the role’s remit.

Global Crypto Business & Financial Support

  • Coordinate with relevant functions to maintain accurate records and resolve business and financial discrepancies.
  • Contribute to control enhancements, process improvements and the development of relevant business requirements.

Work closely with researchers who own live strategies, and together, turn models into P&L.

Overview

As a Quantitative Researcher you'll bring nonlinear and deep learning methods to signal construction across our crypto trading. The scope is deliberately open. Our research agenda spans short-horizon signals that drive market making through to medium-frequency time-series and cross-sectional alphas, and we will shape your focus around where your methods add the most value. You will work closely with researchers who own live strategies, and together you will turn models into P&L.

What you'll be doing

Modeling

  • Design and train tree ensembles and neural networks suited to sequences, order books and cross-sectional panels
  • Benchmark every model against a strong linear baseline, and show where nonlinearity adds value after costs and where it doesn't

Features and representations

  • Build features and learned representations from order books, trades, funding, basis and our own trading flow
  • Test how they hold up across regimes, instruments and venues

Validation and tooling

  • Build training and validation workflows with walk-forward testing, purging and leakage control
  • Contribute reusable model components and evaluation tools to shared research libraries

From model to trade

  • Work with strategy owners to turn model outputs into signals, quote skew, sizing and hedging inputs
  • Measure live impact and take what production shows back into the next model

The ideal candidate

Machine learning depth

  • Hands-on experience applying nonlinear and neural network methods to trading or signal construction, at any horizon
  • Depth in at least one family of architectures suited to financial data, such as sequence, attention-based or order book models, and a clear view of why it fits the problem
  • Experience training models on GPUs with a deep learning framework, and comfort with large datasets

Financial data

  • A grasp of what makes market data hard for machine learning: low signal-to-noise, non-stationarity and leakage
  • Experience with market data in crypto, equities or futures

How you work

  • Skepticism toward your own results, and the ability to explain a failed model as clearly as a working one
  • Willingness to let the simpler model win
  • Clear communication with the researchers who will trade what you build

A live P&L track record isn't required. We assess technical depth and research judgment directly.

Caladan is a principal trading firm specializing in digital assets. We support exchanges, tokens, and institutional investors with market-making, tailored API liquidity, OTC options, and investments. Founded in 2017, we have traded continuously through every market cycle, powering over $170B in annual volume across 1000+ assets.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Ramp is hiring a Manager, CSM, New Products to build and lead the team that helps customers put our newest products to work. This team supports customers across segments. Its job is to take a new product from sales handoff through implementation, first useful result, and early adoption, then make sure the next owner has a clear path forward.

The products and customer needs will change. You will build a team and an operating rhythm that can change with them. You will coach people with different strengths, help them make good decisions when the playbook is still being written, and turn what we learn from customers into a better way to launch the next one. You will work closely with Sales, core Customer Success, Solutions, Product, and Operations to make the customer experience feel coordinated.

What You'll Do

  • Hire, onboard, coach, and develop a growing team of Customer Activation Managers. Set a clear bar for customer judgment, implementation ownership, follow-through, and communication.

  • Give direct, useful feedback through customer-call reviews, case discussions, one-on-ones, and development plans. Help strong individual contributors grow into broader scope and address performance gaps early.

  • Help the team turn an unclear sales handoff into a customer plan with the right stakeholders, prerequisites, owners, milestones, and first useful outcome. Step in on complex launches and escalations when your judgment will move the work forward.

  • Build and improve the team's implementation process: assignment and handoff, customer discovery, launch plans, specialist engagement, first-use checks, adoption follow-up, and the transition to ongoing ownership.

  • Make ownership clear when a customer has both a core Customer Success Manager and a New Products specialist. Keep one customer plan while giving the specialist room to lead the product implementation.

  • Use customer progress, launch quality, team capacity, and time spent on implementations to spot where customers or team members are getting stuck. Adjust coverage and process based on what the data and customer work show.

  • Partner with Sales, Product, Solutions, Support, and Customer Success leaders to resolve recurring blockers, set realistic customer expectations, and improve product readiness and the next launch.

  • Bring early customer patterns back to Product and leadership. Be specific about what customers can do today, what takes specialist help, and what we need to change before the motion scales.

  • Build a team culture where people take ownership, ask for help early, share what they learn, and keep improving the work.

What You'll Need

  • Either 2+ years directly managing a customer success, implementation, solutions, or consulting team or 6+ years as an individual contributor in one or more of those roles, with clear evidence that you have coached others and led work beyond your own accounts.

  • A record of taking customers through a complex implementation or workflow change, from discovery and planning to first use and adoption. You know how to tell whether a customer is actually using what was launched.

  • Experience building or improving a process that other people used, with examples of what you changed after seeing it work in practice.

  • Strong coaching judgment. You can diagnose whether someone needs clearer expectations, better skills, more support, or a change in approach, and you can give feedback that improves performance.

  • Comfort making coverage and prioritization decisions with incomplete information. You can balance customer complexity, team capacity, and product readiness without losing sight of the customer's outcome.

  • The ability to work across Sales, Product, Solutions, and Customer Success when ownership is shared or a customer issue has no obvious answer.

  • Clear communication with customers, individual contributors, and senior leaders. You can explain a risk, make a recommendation, and identify the next owner and step.

  • Curiosity about new products and enough technical and finance fluency to ask good questions, challenge a launch plan, and bring in the right expert. You do not need to be the specialist for every product the team supports.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience building a new post-sale team or launching an implementation motion before the playbook was mature.

  • Experience supporting both high-touch implementations and lighter-weight activation paths across different customer segments.

Europe or United States, remote first with offices available · Full-time · Engineering · Reports to the CTO

About DFNS

Finance is moving onchain. Stablecoins, tokenized deposits, securities and funds are changing how money and assets are issued, held and transferred. The destination is a financial system where any asset can be issued, moved and governed onchain with the controls regulated institutions require. That shift needs a new foundation. Just as core banking systems manage accounts and ledgers today, financial institutions need a platform to manage digital assets. DFNS is that platform. Today, we secure hundreds of billions of dollars in assets every month for more than 500 clients worldwide.

Why this role

Our clients put DFNS in front of their administrators and end users through mobile, where a passkey, a signing approval or a policy decision has to be fast, secure and obvious. You will lead mobile at DFNS, owning the iOS and Android apps and the SDKs clients embed in their own, and bringing fintech UX and bank-level security together on a phone. In year one you will ship the apps our clients rely on, make the SDKs the fastest way to put DFNS inside a client’s app and set the architecture the rest of mobile is built on.

What you’ll do

  • Lead the design and development of our iOS and Android apps, owning features from idea to launch to iteration.

  • Refine the mobile SDKs and cross-platform frameworks clients embed so an integration takes days rather than weeks.

  • Bring fintech UX and bank-level security together on mobile, with WebAuthn, passkeys and secure authentication done right.

  • Set and hold the standards for performance, security and architecture across the mobile stack.

  • Partner with Product and Design to turn complex workflows into simple ones for administrators and end users.

  • Write clear documentation, review code and raise the level of everyone who touches mobile.

  • Work with Product Security so mobile stays a hardened surface rather than the easiest way in.

What you bring

Must-haves

  • A record of leading and shipping production mobile apps in fintech, onchain or another environment where reliability and security were not optional.

  • Expert React Native, with native depth (Swift or Kotlin) for when the framework is not enough.

  • Hands-on experience with WebAuthn, passkeys and secure authentication flows on mobile.

  • Experience building and maintaining SDKs or cross-platform frameworks that other teams integrate.

  • A sharp eye for UX and product detail. You notice the delayed transition and the misaligned button.

  • Ownership of mobile architecture decisions, with the judgment to keep the stack simple.

  • Clear written communication across time zones.

Nice-to-haves

  • Mobile security hardening (jailbreak and root detection, secure storage, certificate pinning).

  • Experience with wallets, key management or signing on device.

  • Design systems and accessibility on mobile.

How we work

We are a distributed company headquartered in Paris. Our teams work from Europe, the US and Asia, with offices in New York, Geneva, Dubai, Singapore, Hong Kong and São Paulo. We write decisions down so they survive time zones. We hold our own work to the standards our clients are held to. We hire people who can own an outcome end to end and we give them the room to do it.

What we offer

A competitive base salary set by role and location, a bonus or variable plan where the role carries one and stock options vesting over four years. Healthcare, flexible vacation, parental leave and a one-time home technology allowance, with travel expenses covered. A MacBook and the equipment you need to do your best work. Remote first, with an office if you want one.

Base salary range: $120,000 to $200,000

Hiring process

We aim to complete the process in 2 weeks and we tell you where you stand after every step.

  • Intro call with Co-CEO (30 minutes).

  • Personality and cognitive assessments, completed on your own time (45 minutes).

  • A technical take-home exercise

  • Focus Interviews (about 2.5 hours): code review (45 minutes), architecture review (45 minutes), cross function (30 minutes) and security best practices (30 minutes).

  • Reference calls and background checks.

Equal opportunity

DFNS is an equal opportunity employer and considers every applicant based on ability and potential, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age or any other characteristic protected by law. If you need an accommodation at any point in the process, tell us and we will arrange it.

  • Strong writing, analytical and communications skills. Must be able to execute tasks within tight deadlines.
  • Strong interpersonal skills are necessary to work effectively with colleagues across regions and business units
  • Should be a self-starter, organized, detail oriented, and results driven

  • Knowledge with AML/CFT/Sanctions, money transmission regulations, and industry best practices.

  • Relevant industry certifications, e.g. CAMS.

This is the first compliance hire for our North American businesses: a Canadian and a US money services business in a regulated payments group. You will hold three roles at both entities: Compliance Officer, Risk Officer, and Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO). The job is to build the programs, then run them.
 
Both businesses are early. They move money across borders for business clients, with foreign exchange where needed, and their volumes are starting now. You will work with a small team and can bring in outside providers for monitoring and reviews, working under your direction. You will report to David.

As Compliance Officer (both entities)

  • Build, then keep current, each entity's written compliance program, with policies approved by a senior officer: client and beneficial-ownership due diligence, enhanced measures for higher-risk clients, record keeping, travel-rule data and training.
  • Assess money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions-evasion risk across clients, products, delivery channels and geographies, and assess new products, payment rails and corridors before launch.
  • Set the outside compliance provider's scope, review its work and sign off what it produces.
  • Run the written, ongoing training program and its training plan for staff and anyone acting for the entities.
  • Keep each entity's registrations current: the money services business registration with FINTRAC and the payment service provider registration with the Bank of Canada in Canada; the FinCEN registration in the US, renewed every two years and re-filed within 180 days of a triggering change.
  • Lead regulator examinations and requests for information, and answer due-diligence requests from banks, payout partners and clients.
  • Monitor state money transmission licensing requirements for the US entity's activity, and advise the business before it enters a new state or product.

As MLRO (both entities)

  • Run transaction monitoring and sanctions screening, and decide every escalated alert.
  • Canada: file suspicious transaction reports with FINTRAC as soon as practicable after reasonable grounds to suspect are established, and terrorist property reports; oversee the prescribed reports, including international electronic funds transfers and virtual currency receipts of C$10,000 or more.
  • US: file suspicious activity reports with FinCEN for suspicious transactions of US$2,000 or more within 30 days of initial detection, and keep them with their supporting documents for five years; oversee currency transaction reporting and OFAC blocking and reject reporting.
  • Act as the contact for law enforcement requests and production orders, and protect the confidentiality of every report.

As Risk Officer (both entities)

  • Canada: act as the senior officer who oversees the written risk management and incident response framework under the Retail Payment Activities Regulations, its incident reports and its third-party risk, and any safeguarding-of-funds framework if end-user funds are held.
  • Canada: file the annual report to the Bank of Canada by March 31, and give notice of a significant change or new activity at least five business days before it happens.
  • Maintain each entity's risk register and risk appetite, covering compliance, operational, third-party and partner risk, and report it to the board.
  • Commission the independent reviews: FINTRAC's effectiveness review at least every two years, the Bank of Canada framework review at least every three years, and the US program's independent review; track every finding to closure.

Must have

  • At least 7 years in anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance at money services businesses, payment companies or the payments arm of a bank, including 3 or more as a compliance officer, MLRO or deputy.
  • Deep knowledge of Canada's Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and FINTRAC's guidance, and working knowledge of the Retail Payment Activities Act.
  • Has built a compliance program, not only run one: written its policies, risk assessment and training plan.
  • Has decided on and filed suspicious transaction reports, and has run transaction monitoring and sanctions screening.
  • Has taken a business through a FINTRAC, bank-partner or audit examination and closed the findings.
  • Due diligence on business clients, including clients that pay out for their own customers, and on banks and payout partners.
  • A recognised AML certification, such as CAMS, or equivalent experience.
  • Writes clearly for boards, regulators and banks, and works alone across time zones.
  • Can pass the background checks regulators and banking partners require.

Can be learned here, or nice to have

  • The US Bank Secrecy Act, FinCEN reporting and OFAC sanctions. Specialist support is available while you learn the US regime.
  • Operational risk and incident response frameworks.
  • Cross-border business payments with foreign exchange, or payments funded in stablecoins or other virtual currency, including the travel rule.
  • US state money transmission licensing.
  • Payout corridors in Asia-Pacific.
  • Has managed outsourced compliance providers or set up monitoring and screening tools.
  • Has been the officer of more than one entity at once.

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

The Solutions Architecture Team partners with our users to realize their full potential through the adoption of prescriptive solutions that drive their growth and success. We influence revenue growth across Stripe’s product portfolio, and collaborate with sales, support, product management, and Stripe’s executive team to provide the best experience to our most valued customers. 

What you’ll do

As a member of the team, the Solutions Architect will build highly consultative trusted relationships with c-level executives and technical decision makers in the customer’s organization to provide business and technical thought leadership, and become a trusted advisor in solving mission-critical business challenges. She/he will architect business models with them so they can drive new monetization opportunities and growth for both the user and Stripe. 

Responsibilities

  • Lead Technical Strategy & Sales:
    • Guide users  through a discovery process to understand their business needs and design a strong, technically feasible solution.
    • Secure the technical win by giving compelling presentations, demonstrations, and executive briefings that show how the product solves the customer's specific problems.
    • Identify and close new complex opportunities, and accelerate solution adoption. Understand and align with the customer’s product and business roadmap and uncover opportunities for Stripe to accelerate their progress on that roadmap. 
  • Drive Account Growth & Expansion:
    • Find and articulate opportunities to grow the product's use within existing accounts, extending its footprint into new global markets or business units.
    • Close complex deals and accelerate the adoption of new features and products.
    • Participate in sales forecasting, Quarterly Business Reviews and account/territory planning to strategically and tactically align for success
  • Serve as a Trusted Advisor:
    • Partner closely with Account Executives as the key technical counterpart to the Sales Executive, providing strategic and architectural guidance to both new and existing users

  • Team Collaboration:

    • Collaborate closely with Account Executives, Professional Services, Customer Success Managers, Partners, Technical Account Managers and Product Teams to develop and execute on the account strategy for Stripe’s platform prospects.

You have achieved an experienced position as an enterprise architect, senior solution architect or solution engineer and have a successful track record advising enterprise-grade digital native / SAAS / Platform / Marketplace companies, focused on identifying business priorities, formulating technology strategies and designing an end-to-end business solution.   • Passion to take on ownership and drive change in a constantly evolving environment.
